# Policy Manifesto Summary

## Family and Education
The document proposes tax relief for families with young children, including increased child tax credits and allowances for married couples with children under 11. For education, it advocates giving schools more autonomy from central bureaucracy, allowing headteachers control over admissions and discipline, enabling successful schools to expand, and permitting new schools to be established by faith communities and parent groups. University funding would be reformed through endowments, with graduate loan repayment thresholds raised to £20,000 annual income.

## Crime and Justice
The manifesto calls for increased police numbers, reduced bureaucracy to allow officers more time on patrol, and expanded secure centres for young offenders. It proposes "honest sentencing" where served time matches court sentences, mandatory imprisonment for drug dealers selling to minors, and enhanced victim rights including designated contact officers and notification of case progress.

## Economy and Taxation
Economic policy centres on £8 billion in targeted tax reductions funded through administrative savings, including abolishing taxes on savings, cutting fuel duty by 6p per litre, and raising pensioner tax allowances. The document proposes annual reductions in regulatory burdens on businesses, transparent government accounts, and retention of the national currency rather than adopting the euro.

## Healthcare
NHS reforms would remove political interference from clinical decisions, introduce maximum waiting times based on medical need, allow patients to choose their hospital, and enable treatment in private facilities when NHS waiting times exceed guarantees. Ward sisters would receive authority over patient care standards.

## Pensions and Elderly Care
Proposals include raising the basic state pension, increasing age-related tax allowances to remove one million pensioners from income tax, abolishing compulsory annuity purchases at 75, and protecting savings of those requiring long-term care.

## Rural and Urban Policy
Rural measures include support for countryside recovery, reduced business rates for village services, and reformed agricultural policies. Urban regeneration would be driven by local companies with powers to improve policing, education, and housing. Regional development agencies would be abolished, returning responsibilities to local councils.

## Governance
Constitutional reforms would restrict voting on England-only matters to relevant MPs, strengthen parliamentary scrutiny, reduce ministerial numbers, and abolish regional assemblies while empowering local councils with greater autonomy.
